generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The condition `(ipv6[0] == (byte) 0xfe && ipv6[1] == (byte) 0x80)` checks if the address is link-local, but it only checks the first two bytes. This might not be sufficient to determine if an IPv6 address is link-local, as the full condition should also check that all subsequent bytes up to the interface identifier are zero except for the last 64 bits. Consider using `Inet6Address.isLinkLocalAddress()` method instead.

The test case `testAddressNotIncludeScopeId` does not verify that the scope ID is indeed not included in the resulting `InetSocketAddress`. It should assert that the scope ID part is absent from the host name representation.
The test case `testLinkOnlyAddressIncludeScopeId` assumes that the scope ID will be represented as `%0` in the host name, which might not always be true depending on how the system formats the address. Consider using `Inet6Address.getScopedInterface()` to verify the scope ID directly.

review_comment: Reading through the man page, it sounds like scope is _only_ supported for link-local addresses. Does that means we should omit the scope, even non-zero scope, if the address is not link local?
I asked myself the same but then decided against it as we should only fill it with non-zero when the underlying OS tells us so..
